title: Corporate earnings soared in Q2, with AI as the 'growth engine': Chart of the Day
excerpt: Roughly 80% of S&P 500 companies that have reported earnings showed positive year-on-year EPS growth.
content_html:
As the second quarter earnings season begins to wind down, Wall Street and Main Street alike are tallying up the scores, and the numbers have been unquestionably strong.

With just under 90% of companies in the S&P 500 (^GSPC) having released second quarter earnings, roughly 80% have reported year-on-year EPS growth, putting the quarter in the 94th percentile for the metric, per Bank of America research.

Those results, plus Wall Street consensus forecasts for the third and fourth quarters, put the S&P 500 on track for four consecutive quarters of EPS growth exceeding 20%, per BofA, a phenomenon that has only happened 10 times since 1936.

Part of that story, according to Bank of America strategists led by Savita Subramanian, is the AI boom that has largely been driving the US equity market.

The second quarter has seen broad earnings growth, with 10 out of 11 sectors on pace for positive year-on-year movement, BofA noted. Yet, "even so, AI remained the index's primary growth engine," the strategists wrote. While the median AI-related stock notched EPS growth of 28%, the median non-AI-related stock saw growth of just 12%.

But that strength isn't likely to last forever, the strategists said. While consensus expectations remain strong for the third and fourth quarters, EPS growth is expected to decelerate in 2027, which the strategists said may muddle investors' perceptions.

The question for investors now is what happens when that torrential growth slows down.

"Markets tend to become less supportive as earnings growth decelerates, with years of above-trend but slowing EPS growth typically producing weaker equity returns," the strategists wrote.

Apollo Global Management's Torsten Sløk made the same point over the weekend, with data pointing out that while profit margins have been steadily surging in the tech sector, everywhere else in the market has seen little to no profit margin expansion — another sign of how dependent the major indexes have become on the AI boom for their returns. (Disclosure: Yahoo is a portfolio company of funds managed by affiliates of Apollo Global Management.)

"The bottom line is that the AI capex boom is so far only showing up in the sellers' margins, not the buyers'," Sløk wrote. "This is important because the longer it takes the S&P 493 to generate ROI, the bigger the downside risks to an economy and a market this concentrated in the AI trade."

That doesn't mean there isn't still a good amount of optimism on Wall Street,

On Monday, JPMorgan Chase's equity strategy team, led by Dubravko Lakos-Bujas, raised their year-end S&P 500 target to 8,000 from 7,800, which, if reached, would mark a roughly 3% appreciation from where the index closed on Friday.

content_html_zh:
随着第二季度财报季开始结束，华尔街和大街都在统计分数，而且数字无疑是强劲的。

根据美国银行的研究，标准普尔 500 指数 (^GSPC) 中有近 90% 的公司发布了第二季度收益，大约 80% 的公司报告了每股收益同比增长，使该季度处于该指标的第 94 个百分位数。

根据美国银行的数据，这些结果加上华尔街对第三季度和第四季度的一致预测，标普 500 指数有望连续四个季度每股收益增长超过 20%，而这种现象自 1936 年以来只发生过 10 次。

Savita Subramanian 领导的美国银行策略师表示，这个故事的一部分是人工智能的繁荣，这在很大程度上推动了美国股市的发展。

美国银行指出，第二季度盈利大幅增长，11 个行业中有 10 个行业的盈利同比出现积极增长。 然而，“即便如此，人工智能仍然是该指数的主要增长引擎，”策略师写道。 虽然人工智能相关股票的每股收益中位数增长了 28%，但非人工智能相关股票的中位数增长仅为 12%。

但策略师表示，这种强势不太可能永远持续下去。 尽管市场对第三季度和第四季度的普遍预期依然强劲，但每股收益增长预计将在 2027 年放缓，策略师表示，这可能会扰乱投资者的看法。

现在投资者面临的问题是，当这种迅猛增长放缓时会发生什么。

策略师写道：“随着盈利增长放缓，市场的支持力度往往会减弱，多年来高于趋势但放缓的每股收益增长通常会导致股票回报率下降。”

阿波罗全球管理公司 (Apollo Global Management) 的托斯顿·斯洛克 (Torsten Sløk) 周末也表达了同样的观点，数据显示，虽然科技行业的利润率一直在稳步上升，但市场上其他地方的利润率几乎没有增长，这也是主要指数对人工智能繁荣的依赖程度的另一个迹象。 （披露：雅虎是一家由阿波罗全球管理公司附属公司管理的基金的投资组合公司。）

Sløk 写道：“最重要的是，迄今为止，人工智能资本支出的繁荣仅体现在卖方的利润中，而不是买方的利润中。” “这一点很重要，因为标准普尔 493 产生投资回报率所需的时间越长，经济体和集中在人工智能行业的市场的下行风险就越大。”

这并不意味着华尔街仍然缺乏乐观情绪，

周一，由杜布拉夫科·拉科斯-布贾斯 (Dubravko Lakos-Bujas) 领导的摩根大通股票策略团队将标准普尔 500 指数年终目标从 7,800 点上调至 8,000 点，如果达到该目标，则该指数将较上周五收盘价上涨约 3%。
